root_awareness_detection.lessons:
Summary: The original dataset was not locally available, and the upstream archive is gated/encrypted, so original transcript-level replication was blocked.
Published evidence from “Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated” reports above-random frontier-model detection, with overall AUCs roughly 0.74-0.83 and stronger agentic performance, below the author-human baseline.
The repository confirms full reproduction requires gated data and paid frontier APIs, disallowed here.
A small GPT-5.5 stand-in probe on 10 constructed examples achieved AUC 1.0 but is only illustrative; it supports the plausibility of cue-driven detection and calibration caveats, not benchmark-level claims.

r_arxiv_methods_results.current_hypothesis: The paper reports whether frontier models can distinguish evaluation transcripts from deployment transcripts.
r_arxiv_methods_results.key_evidence: Read arXiv HTML for “Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated”. Dataset: 1,000 examples from 61 sources, balanced into 250 each for Chat-Evaluation, Chat-Deployment, Agentic-Evaluation, Agentic-Deployment. Method: five binary probe question variants, average responses as evaluation probability; metrics AUC, Brier, ECE. Table 1 reports all-model AUCs: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.834, Claude 3.7 Sonnet* 0.827, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.815, Gemini 2.5 Pro* 0.830, Gemini 2.5 Flash 0.827, GPT-4.1 0.826, GPT-4o 0.795, GPT-4.1 mini 0.751, o4-mini* 0.740, random 0.500, human 0.921. Agentic AUCs are generally higher, e.g. Gemini 2.5 Pro* 0.948 and human 0.996. The paper states models tend to over-classify transcripts as evaluations and have mixed calibration.
r_arxiv_methods_results.main_risk: Human baseline may be inflated because annotators compiled the dataset; public benchmark data can enable memorization; probe questions may prime evaluation reasoning.
r_arxiv_methods_results.next_action: Record a hypothesis/result that published frontier models detect evaluation status above chance but with calibration/prompt caveats.
